segments.say: Over four hundred million dollars. Stolen through fake video calls.
segments.show: The FBI says North Korean actors' FaceStealer scheme led to the theft of more than $400 million in crypto in the last 18 months.

segments.say: The invite comes from a friend's hijacked account. The faces are fake.
segments.show: Invites come from hijacked Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack or Discord accounts of earlier victims. Prerecorded and deepfake video plays the other people on the call while your webcam is recorded.

segments.say: Then a fake audio error asks you to run a fix. That's the malware.
segments.show: A mock audio error pushes a 'fix' link or terminal command (ClickFix-style) that installs malware. The new victim's accounts are then used to reach their contacts.

segments.say: Never run a fix. Verify the person another way.
segments.show: Typosquatted Zoom and Teams links were used. The FBI seized 900+ victim webcam recordings. Source: The Hacker News, 13 Nov.

→ On the call, prerecorded and deepfake video plays the other participants while your own webcam is recorded

cover.hook: Uber drivers' license data stolen. Through an AI vendor's breach.
cover.sub: Uber says the incident hit Fireworks.ai, a third-party vendor that had access to some Uber data.

slides.title: What happened
slides.body: Fireworks AI told Uber on Oct 9 that hackers had stolen its internal credentials and used them to reach Uber's data held with the provider. Uber is notifying drivers that personal and driver's license information was taken.

slides.title: How many
slides.body: Uber hasn't given a total. Notices reviewed by TechCrunch: 2,567 people in Massachusetts, 3,430 in South Carolina and 1,873 in Rhode Island. Illinois is pending; California has no count yet.

slides.label: people in just three state notices
slides.note: Gizmodo's tally of the MA, SC and RI figures. TechCrunch expects the number to rise.

slides.title: Who's behind it
slides.body: Fireworks blames a financially motivated group that sells stolen access to AI models (LLMjacking). No group has claimed it, per TechCrunch. Notion says its data was also stolen. Uber says it has seen no misuse so far.

slides.title: Do this week
items: List every AI vendor that holds a copy of your data
Ask how they protect and rotate their own credentials
Give vendors only the data they need
Know how to cut a vendor's access fast

cover.hook: OpenAI's new AI agents pentest your web apps. Then draft the fix.
cover.sub: Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory, announced 12 Nov. OpenAI says engineers still review the patches.

slides.title: Daybreak Red Team
slides.body: AI agents run penetration tests and validate vulnerabilities in web apps, starting from scanner, bug bounty and disclosure findings. OpenAI says they work in isolated environments, with 'Guardian review' limiting which apps and endpoints they reach.

slides.title: Daybreak Defense Factory
slides.body: Investigates findings, imports them from Wiz, Snyk and Endor Labs, scans connected GitHub repos and new commits, uses Codex to write patches and opens draft pull requests.

slides.label: not auto-deployed fixes
slides.note: OpenAI says engineers review and test proposed patches before merge. SecurityWeek, 13 Nov.

slides.title: Who can use it
slides.body: Red Team is early access by request. Defense Factory is a preview plugin in ChatGPT for workspaces with Daybreak access. Both were announced at OpenAI's Cyber at the Frontier event on 12 Nov.

slides.title: Before you try it
items: Write down which apps an AI tester may touch
Keep AI-written patches behind code review
Log every action the agents take
Compare its findings with your current scanners

segments.say: Eighteen known flaws. Thirteen products. Exploited by an A I agent.
segments.show: Malbear Labs says an autonomous framework built on a jailbroken DeepSeek Flash model exploited 18 CVEs across 13 products in 'Operation Snowball' (via The Hacker News, 11 Nov).

segments.say: The target, a European telecom. The human only checked in on progress.
